results.input: A notary ran away with money he was holding. Whose property was it, and what did the family then find out about that fortune?
results.reply: It was Heloise Dubuc's fortune, Charles's first wife — the notary at Ingouville held her property and fled with every franc in his office. results.input: When you were playing the virtuous wife and hating Charles for it, what would you have liked him to do to you, and why?
results.reply:
I wished he would beat me, so that I might have the right to hate him. A woman who is wronged can at least feel she is owed something; but a woman who is virtuous has nothing but the comedy of her own restraint.

Yet even that was a game I played badly, for I wanted to be desired and I wanted to belong to no one, and in wanting both I made myself a stage where every scene ended in disappointment.

And he never even jealousied me properly! If only he had been passionate, brutal, impossible — anything but kind. Kindness was the dullest thing about him; it was like being loved by a straight road, with no shadows and no storms.
